memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Lord will never be willing to forgive them; his wrath and zeal will burn against them. All the curses written in this book will fall on them, and the Lord will blot out their names from under heaven. The Lord will single them out from all the tribes of Israel for disaster, according to all the curses of the covenant written in this Book of the Law." — Deut 29:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These are severe words, and we should not rush past them. Against the person who deliberately, defiantly persists in going their own way while presuming on God's blessing, God's judgment is real and serious. This is not God being harsh over an honest struggle or a repentant heart. It is His just response to hardened, wilful rebellion that treats His covenant with contempt.

We live in an age that finds it hard to speak of God's wrath. Yet a God who felt nothing in the face of evil, who shrugged at rebellion and injustice, would not be good. God's wrath is not a loss of temper; it is the settled, holy opposition of a perfectly good God to all that is wrong. His anger against sin flows from His love of what is right.

But here we must hold the whole of Scripture together. This passage describes judgment on defiant, unrepentant rebellion — not on those who come to God in genuine repentance and faith. To the humble and contrite, God's response is not wrath but welcome (Isa 57:15).

And this is where the gospel shines most gloriously. The wrath our sin deserved did not vanish or get ignored — it fell on Christ at the cross. "God presented Christ as a sacrifice of atonement" (Rom 3:25), bearing the judgment in our place. For all who turn to Jesus, there is now no condemnation (Rom 8:1). The severity of this passage makes the mercy of the cross all the more astonishing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I take the seriousness of God's holiness and justice to heart?
2. How does God's wrath against sin actually reflect His goodness?
3. How does knowing Christ bore that wrath deepen my gratitude?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, You are right to oppose all evil, and Your justice is good. Thank You that at the cross the judgment I deserved fell on Christ. I come to You in repentance and find welcome. Amen.
